claims.text: As-received Q235 steel has an intact native room-temperature iron-oxide film.
High-temperature molten-salt corrosion of pre-exposed Q235 steel is governed primarily by instability and poor adhesion of its native oxide scale.
At room temperature, the native film on Q235 steel acts as a passivating barrier.
At 700–900 °C, the native film fails through dissolution, spallation, or phase transformation.
Failure of the native film at 700–900 °C exposes Q235 steel and accelerates metal loss.
The relevant native scale consists primarily of magnetite or mixed iron oxides.
At room temperature, the native oxide is coherent, dense, and adhesive and therefore limits metal dissolution.
High thermal energy and differential thermal expansion destabilize the Q235 oxide scale during high-temperature exposure.
Salt-induced fluxing dissolves or spalls the oxide scale during high-temperature molten-salt exposure.
The persistence or failure of corrosion protection is directly controlled by oxide-scale integrity.
Relative to alloyed stainless steel, Q235 steel should exhibit low mass change and an intact oxide scale during room-temperature salt exposure.
Relative to alloyed stainless steel, Q235 steel should exhibit marked mass loss, disrupted or spalled oxide, and uneven morphology after salt exposure at 700–900 °C.
A stainless steel containing deliberately alloyed passivating elements is a stable reference system under the proposed exposures.
Controlling oxygen partial pressure prevents uncontrolled oxidation and isolates the role of temperature in oxide-scale stability.
The proposed oxide-instability mechanism is expected to apply to untreated, non-alloyed, and non-coated Q235 steel.
Surface treatments, alloying, or coatings can alter corrosion behavior sufficiently that the proposed native-oxide mechanism might not apply.
Mn dissolution into molten salt can establish an Mn/MnF2 redox buffer or sacrificial mechanism that reduces Cr dissolution.
HEA coatings can be deposited on conventional substrates to exploit the coatings' performance advantages.

contradictions.description: The study is said to isolate thermal effects, but the high-temperature specimens experience molten salt while the room-temperature specimens experience an aqueous salt solution. Temperature, salt phase, solvent chemistry, water activity, and likely electrochemical conditions therefore change together.
